key_insight: A large portion of token-to-token attention connections in spatiotemporal transformers produce negligible scores repeatedly; by detecting and skipping these connections with a calibrated sparse-mask, text-to-video diffusion models can avoid much attention computation with little to no quality loss.
problem_solved: Transformer-based spatiotemporal attention is a major runtime bottleneck in text-to-video diffusion models, causing slow inference and high compute cost.
method: Detect repeated low-score token-to-token connections across inputs/queries and construct sparse attention masks to skip unnecessary attention computations.
Calibrate the sparsity (e.g., via thresholds or lightweight corrective steps) to retain fidelity and avoid degradation in generated video quality.
Plug calibrated sparse attention into the diffusion model backbone so spatiotemporal attention is computed only for the most relevant token pairs during generation.
impact: Significantly reduces inference latency and compute for text-to-video generation, enabling faster experimentation, larger models, or near-real-time applications while maintaining output quality.
visual_elements: Attention heatmap before vs after sparsification (masked negligible connections dimmed/removed)
Bar chart: runtime (or FLOPs) reduction vs minimal change in quality metric (e.g., FID/LPIPS)

Side-by-side generated frame sequences: dense attention vs calibrated sparse attention (visual parity)
paper_title: Accelerating Text-to-Video Generation with Calibrated Sparse Attention
paper_authors: Shai Yehezkel, Shahar Yadin, Noam Elata, Yaron Ostrovsky-Berman, Bahjat Kawar
